intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, dramatic limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos port.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets in Monastiraki. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional street foods like souvlaki and spanakopita. Engage with local vendors and discover authentic Greek flavors that tourists rarely experience.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand caused by crushed coral and shells. Wade through shallow crystal-clear lagoons to reach the small island of Elafonissi. Bring a picnic of local bread, feta, and olives from a nearby village market for a perfect beach day.

experiences.name: Traditional Taverna Dinner in Plaka
experiences.description: Enjoy an authentic Greek dinner at a family-run taverna in the historic Plaka neighborhood beneath the Acropolis. Feast on mezedes such as tzatziki, dolmades, grilled octopus, fresh catch of the day, and local wine or ouzo. This is the quintessential Greek dining experience with live traditional music in many establishments.

experiences.name: Santorini Caldera Sunset & Wine Tasting
experiences.description: Watch the world-famous Santorini sunset from the cliffside village of Oia while sampling local Assyrtiko white wine and Vinsanto dessert wine produced from volcanic soil grapes. Visit a local winery or a cliffside wine bar for a tasting session paired with local cheeses and cherry tomatoes grown on the island.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities – flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities – flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange budget transfer (airport bus or shared shuttle) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snack
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport cafe
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night gyro or souvlaki wrap from a nearby street kiosk or 24-hour snack bar close to the hotel (budget-friendly, ~€3–5)

day_by_day.notes: Keep a small amount of euros handy for transport and snacks upon arrival. Don't over-plan tonight – rest is the priority after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take your first stroll along the beachfront promenade right outside Aegean Bliss Resort. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea and soak in the stunning views. Explore the immediate beach area and get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest local village or town on foot or by local bus. Wander through the main square, browse small shops, and visit the local open-air market if available. Pick up fresh fruit, olives, and local snacks for a cheap and delicious picnic lunch on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach – Greece is famous for its golden-hour light. Stroll the waterfront and find a casual taverna for dinner. Look for a place with a handwritten menu board and locals dining inside – a sure sign of authentic, affordable food.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or pick up a tiropita (cheese pie) and Greek coffee from a local bakery (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Self-assembled picnic from the market: fresh bread, olives, feta, tomatoes, and fruit (~€5–7 total)
meals.dinner: Local taverna: grilled sardines or moussaka with a Greek salad and house wine or water (~€10–14)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange or withdraw euros from a local ATM today if needed. Download a local bus app or ask hotel reception for bus schedules to plan future days.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim at the hotel beach before crowds arrive – the sea is warm and crystal clear. Spend time snorkeling if you have gear (cheap snorkel sets available at local shops for ~€10–15). Enjoy the calm morning atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus to a nearby less-touristy beach recommended by hotel staff. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing. Bring water and snacks from a local minimarket to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Explore the local neighborhood on foot and find a small family-run ouzerie (Greek mezze bar). Order a selection of small plates (mezedes) to share – great way to try many local flavors affordably.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local café (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from minimarket: crackers, cheese, fruit, water (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Ouzerie mezedes: tzatziki, dolmades, grilled octopus, and ouzo or local beer (~€12–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Apply high-SPF sunscreen generously – the June sun is very strong at 29°C. Stay hydrated throughout the day. Reusable water bottle recommended to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby ancient archaeological site or historic church/monastery in the region (many have free or low-cost entry). Explore at a leisurely pace and enjoy the history and architecture in the early cool of the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for a long afternoon swim session. Try renting a paddleboard or kayak from a beach rental shop for 1 hour (~€8–12) for some active fun on the water.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or assemble your own meal using ingredients from the local supermarket or market – great budget option. Alternatively, find a souvlaki grill shop (grill house) for cheap and filling takeaway.

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and fresh orange juice from a local bakery (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Souvlaki pita wrap with tzatziki and fries from a local grill shop (~€3–5)
meals.dinner: Supermarket self-catering: pasta, local cheese, olives, tomatoes, and Greek wine (~€8–10 total) OR souvlaki shop dinner (~€6–8)

day_by_day.notes: Many archaeological sites offer free entry on the first Sunday of the month and for EU students year-round. Check in advance for any free entry days.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or shared taxi to a nearby fishing village or harbor town. Walk along the harbor, watch fishermen bring in their catch, and explore the colorful boats and waterfront cafes. This is authentic Greek coastal life at its best.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a long, lazy lunch at a harbourside fish taverna – ask what the fresh catch of the day is for the best value. Spend the rest of the afternoon exploring the village's narrow backstreets, small churches, and local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the resort area. Relax on the beach for the golden-hour sunset. Grab a cheap gyro or street food for a light dinner and enjoy the evening sea breeze on the promenade.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and koulouri (sesame bread ring) from a street vendor (~€2)
meals.lunch: Fresh fish of the day with village salad and bread at a harbour taverna (~€12–16 – splurge slightly for the experience)
meals.dinner: Gyro pita wrap from a street grill shop (~€3–4)

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining is not typical in Greek restaurants, but asking for the 'catch of the day' often gets you fresher fish at a better price. Carry cash as smaller village shops may not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Lazy beach morning – this is a rest and recharge day. Read a book, swim, and enjoy the simple pleasure of the warm Aegean sun. Walk along the shoreline and collect sea glass or shells.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local food market or farmers' market if one operates nearby today. Sample local produce, honey, herbs, and handmade goods. Pick up affordable local specialties like thyme honey, dried herbs, or local olive oil as future souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Find a rooftop or terrace taverna for dinner with a view. Order the house specialty and a carafe of local house wine (barrel wine is very affordable in Greece – often €4–6 for a half-litre carafe).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a simple Greek coffee and toast at a local café (~€3)
meals.lunch: Market snacking: fresh fruit, local cheese, olives, and bread (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Terrace taverna: lamb chops or stuffed peppers with rice, village salad, and house wine (~€13–16)

day_by_day.notes: This is a good day to do laundry if needed. Many budget accommodations have laundry facilities or there are laundromats nearby. Pack light and rewear clothing to save luggage space and money.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby island or coastal area reachable by ferry or local boat. Check with the hotel for affordable day-trip ferry options. Depart early to maximize time. Explore the island's main beach, village, and viewpoints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim and snorkel at the island's clearest beach. Pack your own lunch (sandwiches and fruit from the supermarket) to avoid overpriced tourist restaurants on the island.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry back to the main area. Dinner at a tried-and-true local spot you've already discovered during the trip. Toast to the halfway point of your trip!

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure – yogurt and honey or a pastry from the bakery (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the island beach: sandwiches, fruit, snacks (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Return to a favourite local taverna: souvlaki platter or grilled vegetables with feta and pita (~€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets can often be purchased at the port on the day. Arrive 30–45 minutes early to secure a spot. Bring sunscreen, water, and a small day bag. Wear swimwear under your clothes for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a different beach in the region – ask locals or hotel staff for a hidden or less-crowded gem. Many beautiful Greek beaches are accessible only by a short hike or dirt path, keeping them quieter and more scenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the hidden beach. Swim, relax, and enjoy the solitude. If the path involved a hike, take time to appreciate the coastal scenery and wildflowers along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local bakery or pastry shop (zacharoplasteio) for a sweet treat – try loukoumades (honey donuts), baklava, or galaktoboureko (custard pastry). Light dinner from a grill shop or market.

meals.breakfast: Homemade-style breakfast: buy bread, eggs, tomatoes, and feta from the supermarket and prepare in the hotel room if facilities allow (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at the hidden beach (~€5–6)
meals.dinner: Grill shop: chicken souvlaki plate with pita, tzatziki, and salad (~€7–9)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy sandals or sneakers if hiking to a remote beach. Always carry more water than you think you need in 29°C heat. Let hotel reception know where you're heading for safety.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to a local Byzantine church, hilltop chapel, or historic windmill in the area. These are often free to enter and offer stunning panoramic views. Bring a light scarf or shawl to cover shoulders if required for entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for a swim and relaxation session. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella (~€5–8 for the pair) for a comfortable afternoon. Try reading a local English-language travel guide to learn more about the region.
day_by_day.evening: Seek out a traditional Greek music taverna or a place with live music on certain evenings. Many local restaurants have live bouzouki music on weekends – check with hotel staff for recommendations. Enjoy dinner with the authentic soundtrack of Greece.

meals.breakfast: Freddo cappuccino (iced Greek coffee) and a cheese or ham toast at a local café (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Beach kiosk snack: toasted sandwich, chips, and a cold drink (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Live music taverna: mixed grill plate or pastitsio (Greek baked pasta) with salad and house wine (~€13–16)

day_by_day.notes: Live music venues are often busy on Friday and Saturday evenings. Arrive early to secure a good table. Tipping is appreciated but not mandatory – rounding up the bill is the common practice.

day_by_day.morning: Take a cooking or food experience morning – visit a local market early and pick up ingredients to understand what goes into Greek cuisine. Alternatively, some small guesthouses or local hosts offer informal cooking demonstrations for a small fee (~€15–20).
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon beach time. Try a new water activity – many beaches offer affordable options like pedal boats (~€8–10/hour) or banana boat rides (~€8–10). Alternatively, simply swim and snorkel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local nightlife strip or waterfront bars. Enjoy a pre-dinner drink (local beer or a glass of ouzo with ice and water) at a bar with sea views. Find a casual dinner spot afterward.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with local honey, granola, and fresh figs from a café (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Market-fresh ingredients assembled into a Greek salad and bread meal (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Casual seafood taverna: grilled calamari, horiatiki salad, and a glass of local white wine (~€11–14)

day_by_day.notes: Ouzo is best sipped slowly with water and ice and accompanied by small bites (mezedes). It's a cultural experience as much as a drink. Many bars offer complimentary small snacks with drinks.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longer excursion by local bus or rented bicycle to explore the wider region. Visit a nearby town or village you haven't seen yet. Explore its central square (plateia), local church, and traditional architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a shaded café in the village square and enjoy a long, relaxed Greek lunch. This is the Greek way – lunch is the main meal of the day and is meant to be enjoyed slowly. Rest during the hottest part of the afternoon (2–4 PM) as locals do.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Spend a quiet evening on the beach watching the stars – Greece has very little light pollution in coastal areas, making stargazing spectacular. Pick up a bottle of local wine from a supermarket (~€4–6) and enjoy it on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Simple hotel or café breakfast: bread, butter, jam, and Greek coffee (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Village taverna: slow-cooked lamb or chicken in tomato sauce with rice or potatoes and salad (~€10–13)
meals.dinner: Light evening: supermarket wine, cheese, olives, and bread on the beach (~€6–8)

day_by_day.notes: Bicycle rental is an excellent budget transport option (~€8–12/day) and lets you explore at your own pace. Ask hotel reception for recommended cycling routes that avoid main roads.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit your favourite beach one last time for a long morning swim. This is your penultimate full day – savour the warm Aegean water and the beautiful surroundings. Take photos and absorb the atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping. Best budget souvenirs in Greece: local honey, olive oil, dried oregano, evil eye (mati) charms, and handmade ceramics. Avoid tourist trap shops near major attractions – local markets and village shops have better prices.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on your final full dinner in Greece. Choose a highly-rated local taverna and try dishes you haven't eaten yet on the trip. Order a dessert – Greek sweets like baklava or galaktoboureko are a must-try finale.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at a café: eggs, olives, feta, tomatoes, bread, and coffee (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch: souvlaki pita and a cold drink (~€4–5)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the best local taverna: seafood platter or mixed grill, Greek salad, dessert, and a glass of local wine (~€18–22 – a worthy splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight to make the morning less stressful. Keep one outfit and toiletries accessible for the morning. Confirm your transport to the airport for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Take in the views, breathe the sea air, and say goodbye to the Aegean. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and store luggage with reception if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time permits before departure, enjoy a final coffee and pastry at your favourite local café. Take a last stroll along the promenade. Arrange your transfer to the airport well in advance (budget airport bus or shared shuttle recommended).
day_by_day.evening: Depart for the airport. Arrive at least 2 hours before your flight. Enjoy a final Greek coffee or a small snack at the airport. Board your flight home with a head full of memories, a sun-kissed glow, and a belly full of amazing Greek food.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek coffee and a pastry or koulouri at the beach café (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Airport café or a packed snack from the supermarket (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Greece departure tax is included in most flight tickets. Keep some euros for airport snacks or last-minute purchases. Take a photo of your hotel and beach before you leave – you'll want to remember this place. Καλό ταξίδι! (Have a good trip!)

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort facilities.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon arrival — grab a Greek yogurt with honey or a small mezze plate if the kitchen is still open.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — late arrival means rest is the priority. Confirm your resort transfer in advance and have local currency (euros) ready for tips. Set an alarm for a relaxed start on Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. Take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront promenade near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea for the first time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon settling into beach life — find a sun lounger on the resort beach, swim in the crystal-clear water (sea temperature ideal at this time of year), and explore the immediate coastal area on foot. Visit a nearby beach kiosk for a cold freddo espresso.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest local village for a relaxed first dinner out. Stroll the waterfront and pick a traditional taverna with outdoor seating.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — fresh fruit, Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, spanakopita, and strong Greek coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside café near the resort — try a Greek salad (horiatiki) and a fresh-squeezed orange juice (€10–14).
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in the local village — order grilled octopus, tzatziki, warm pita, and a carafe of local house wine (€20–28 per person).

day_by_day.notes: This is your recovery and settling-in day. Don't over-schedule — let yourself adjust to the heat and time zone. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen generously; the June sun is strong.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and visit a local morning market (laiki agora) nearby to browse fresh produce, olives, cheeses, and local honey. Pick up some snacks for the day. Return to the resort or head to a quiet café for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak or paddleboard from a local water sports rental near the resort beach. Explore the coastline from the water, discovering small coves and sea caves. Swim in a secluded spot accessible only by water.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from a clifftop or elevated point near the resort. Then enjoy dinner at a seafood restaurant by the harbour.

meals.breakfast: Local café breakfast — bougatsa (custard or cheese-filled pastry) and Greek coffee (€5–7).
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach using market finds — olives, local cheese (graviera or feta), bread, tomatoes, and fruit.
meals.dinner: Harbourfront seafood restaurant — fresh grilled fish of the day (priced by weight, approx. €18–25), grilled vegetables, and a glass of Assyrtiko white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Kayak rentals typically cost €15–25 for a half-day. Book in advance during peak season. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water for the water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day guided boat trip to nearby sea caves, hidden beaches, or a small uninhabited island close to the resort area. Many local operators offer morning departures (9:00–13:00). Swim in turquoise waters and snorkel around underwater rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a relaxed afternoon. Lounge by the pool or beach, read, and recharge. Optional: visit the resort spa for a short treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local town's main square (plateia) in the evening — join locals for the traditional evening stroll (volta). Find a mezedopolio (meze restaurant) for a shared-plate dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — eggs, fresh bread, local honey, olives, and fruit.
meals.lunch: Light snack on the boat — bring your own or buy from the boat operator (often included or sold onboard). Cheese pie (tiropita) and water.
meals.dinner: Mezedopolio in town — order 5–6 small plates to share: dolmades, taramosalata, saganaki (fried cheese), grilled halloumi, and loukaniko sausage. Budget €18–24 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Boat trips cost approximately €25–45 per person depending on duration and what's included. Book the day before through the resort concierge or a local tour desk. Bring a towel, snorkel gear if you have it, and motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby archaeological site or historic church/monastery in the morning when it's cooler. Many Greek islands and coastal areas have ancient ruins or Byzantine chapels within easy reach. Hire a local guide or use an audio guide app for context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a popular local beach with clear water and good facilities — rent a sun lounger and umbrella and spend a few hours swimming and relaxing. Try snorkelling along the rocky edges of the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class or food experience in the local area — many villages offer 2–3 hour evening classes teaching traditional Greek dishes. Alternatively, visit a local winery or distillery for a tasting session.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri (sesame bread ring) and a freddo cappuccino from a street vendor or local bakery (€3–5).
meals.lunch: Beachside taverna — try shrimp saganaki (prawns baked in tomato and feta sauce) and a Greek salad (€14–18).
meals.dinner: If attending a cooking class, dinner is the meal you prepare — typically includes appetisers, a main (moussaka or pastitsio), and dessert. If not, choose a local family-run restaurant and try lamb kleftiko (slow-cooked lamb, €16–22).

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes typically cost €45–70 per person and are a fantastic way to connect with local food culture. Book at least 2 days ahead. Wear comfortable shoes for the morning archaeological visit.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a neighbouring island or coastal town via local ferry or water taxi. Explore the main streets, browse local shops, and visit a notable landmark or viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at one of the day-trip destination's famous beaches. Many nearby islands have beaches rated among the best in Greece. Have lunch at a local spot before heading back.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Enjoy a quiet evening — sunset cocktails at the resort bar, then a relaxed dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — fruit, yogurt, and coffee to fuel the day.
meals.lunch: Local taverna at the day-trip destination — fresh fish, village salad, and local bread (€15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or a nearby casual eatery — try moussaka or pastitsio with a glass of local red wine (€18–24).

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance — morning departures are usually 8:00–10:00 and return trips mid-to-late afternoon. Round-trip ferry tickets typically €15–35 depending on distance. Bring a small daypack with sunscreen, water, and a light layer for the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in or do gentle yoga/stretching on the beach at sunrise. Enjoy a long, leisurely breakfast at the resort. This is your mid-trip reset day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area by bicycle or scooter — rent from a shop near the resort and ride along coastal roads, stopping at viewpoints, small chapels, or quiet coves. The terrain is typically manageable for casual riders.
day_by_day.evening: Join a sunset sailing trip (many depart around 17:30–18:00 and last 2–3 hours). Watch the sun dip below the horizon from the water with a drink in hand.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — take your time. Try everything: spanakopita, fresh-squeezed juice, Greek cheeses, and honey.
meals.lunch: Village kafeneion (traditional Greek café) — simple lunch of bread, olives, local cheese, and a cold Mythos or Alfa beer (€8–12).
meals.dinner: Post-sailing dinner at a waterfront restaurant — grilled calamari, dakos (Cretan bruschetta with tomato and feta), and fresh fish (€20–28 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental costs approximately €20–35/day; bicycle €10–15/day. Helmets are required by law. Sunset sailing trips typically cost €35–55 per person. Book sailing in advance through the resort or a local tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local olive oil producer, honey farm, or artisan food producer in the area for a guided tour and tasting. This is a wonderful way to understand the agricultural roots of Greek cuisine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a less-visited, more secluded beach — ask the resort or locals for their hidden gem recommendation. Spend the afternoon swimming, reading, and enjoying the peace away from the crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a highly-rated local restaurant known for modern Greek cuisine — a step up from the everyday taverna but still mid-range in price.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery — fresh tiropita or spanakopita and a strong Greek coffee (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic for the secluded beach — pick up supplies from a local mini-market: bread, hummus, olives, cherry tomatoes, and fruit (€8–12 total).
meals.dinner: Modern Greek restaurant — try dishes like sea bass ceviche with citrus, lamb with kritharaki (orzo), and loukoumades (honey doughnuts) for dessert. Budget €28–38 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Ask your resort concierge to recommend the best local food producers for tours — many are small family operations not widely advertised. The secluded beach may require a short hike (15–30 minutes) so wear appropriate footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning swim before the beach gets busy — the sea is glassy and calm in the early hours. Then visit a local museum, cultural centre, or historic site in the nearest town to add some depth to your understanding of the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a snorkelling or diving excursion with a local dive centre. The Aegean has excellent underwater visibility in June. Beginners can do a discovery dive; experienced divers can explore deeper sites.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the old quarter (if applicable) of the nearest town in the early evening. Browse local craft shops and pick up souvenirs — look for hand-painted ceramics, local honey, or olive oil products.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fuel up before the active day.
meals.lunch: Post-dive meal at a casual harbour-side spot — try a gyros wrap or souvlaki with tzatziki and chips (€8–12).
meals.dinner: Traditional psarotaverna (fish taverna) — whole grilled fish, grilled vegetables, taramasalata, and a carafe of white wine (€22–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Snorkelling trips cost approximately €20–35; introductory dives €55–80; certified dives €40–60. Book through a reputable PADI or SSI certified centre. Museum entry fees are typically €4–10. Afternoons are hottest (30°C+) — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longer excursion to a notable inland village or mountain town in the region. Explore narrow stone-paved streets, Byzantine churches, and traditional architecture. Many such villages offer panoramic views of the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Have lunch in the inland village, then visit a local winery for an afternoon tasting session — Greek wines (Assyrtiko, Xinomavro, Agiorgitiko) are world-class and underappreciated. Return to the resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Low-key evening at the resort — enjoy cocktails at the bar, a swim in the pool at dusk, and dinner at the resort restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Village taverna in the inland town — try slow-cooked goat stew (katsikaki), village salad, and local bread (€14–18).
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — enjoy the convenience and comfort. Try whatever the chef's special is, paired with a Greek wine you discovered at today's tasting (€20–28).

day_by_day.notes: Arrange transport to the inland village in advance — a hired car (€35–50/day) or a local guided tour (€40–60/person) are the best options. Winery tastings typically cost €10–20 per person and include 4–6 wines. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the village exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a full beach morning at the resort's best beach spot. Arrive early to claim a prime location. Swim, snorkel, and soak up the Greek summer sun. Bring a good book.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try a new water sport — windsurfing, stand-up paddleboarding, or parasailing (if available in the area). Many beach resorts have equipment rental and brief lessons available on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cultural event, live music performance, or open-air cinema if one is happening nearby. Greece has a vibrant summer cultural calendar. If nothing is scheduled, find a rooftop bar with sea views for sundowner cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Grab a yogurt parfait and fresh fruit from the resort beach bar — eat with your feet in the sand.
meals.lunch: Beach taverna — try fried zucchini balls (kolokythokeftedes), grilled sardines, and a cold Mythos beer (€12–16).
meals.dinner: Lively local restaurant in town — try a mixed grill platter (souvlaki, lamb chops, sausage) with pita and sides, shared between two. Budget €16–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check local event listings through the resort concierge or the local municipality's tourism website. Water sport rentals vary — budget €20–50 depending on activity. Parasailing is weather-dependent.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning — dedicate it to your favourite activity from the trip. Whether that's an early swim at your favourite beach, a final kayak, or a peaceful café breakfast in the village, make it meaningful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any remaining souvenir shopping — stock up on local olive oil, thyme honey, herbs, ouzo, or hand-made crafts. Visit a local deli or food shop to pick up edible souvenirs to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner at the best restaurant you've discovered on the trip — or a new spot recommended by locals. Dress up slightly and make it a special occasion.

meals.breakfast: Favourite local café — revisit a spot you loved earlier in the trip.
meals.lunch: Light and casual — a gyros or souvlaki from a street stall while shopping (€5–8).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a top-rated local restaurant — splurge slightly on a multi-course meal. Start with mezedes, move to a main of fresh lobster pasta or whole grilled sea bream, and finish with galaktoboureko (custard pastry) and a digestif of local raki or mastiha liqueur. Budget €35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your souvenirs carefully — olive oil and wine bottles need to be well-wrapped. Liquid restrictions apply for carry-on luggage; pack in checked bags. Confirm your departure transfer or taxi for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one last sunrise swim in the Aegean — a perfect final memory of Greece. Return, shower, and enjoy a last Greek breakfast at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your flight time, either head directly to the airport or store luggage at the resort and enjoy a few final hours nearby. Visit a local café for a final freddo espresso and a piece of baklava.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with a full heart, a tan, and a bag full of local treasures. Review your favourite moments and start planning your return trip.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — go back to your favourites: Greek yogurt, honey, fresh fruit, and strong coffee.
meals.lunch: Airport or pre-departure light meal — grab a spanakopita or tiropita from a local bakery near the airport (€4–7).
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport transfer — typically 2–3 hours before international departure. Double-check all belongings including adapters, chargers, and any items left in the hotel safe. Greece's VAT refund (for non-EU travellers) can be claimed at the airport for eligible purchases over €50.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, dramatic limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos port.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets in Monastiraki. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional street foods like souvlaki and spanakopita. Engage with local vendors and discover authentic Greek flavors that tourists rarely experience.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand caused by crushed coral and shells. Wade through shallow crystal-clear lagoons to reach the small island of Elafonissi. Bring a picnic of local bread, feta, and olives from a nearby village market for a perfect beach day.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, welcome amenities, and light room service to settle in comfortably.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at the resort – charcuterie board, Greek mezze platter, and a glass of premium Greek wine to welcome you to Greece

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Resort concierge should be notified of late arrival to ensure smooth check-in and a welcome amenity such as chilled champagne and fresh fruit in the room.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late morning start after last night's arrival. Enjoy a lavish breakfast at the resort's beachfront terrace. Take a slow stroll along the private beach, dip into the warm Aegean Sea, and get oriented with the resort's premium facilities including infinity pool and spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate coastal surroundings. Rent a private boat or join a curated small-group boat excursion along the local coastline to discover hidden coves and crystal-clear bays. Snorkeling gear provided. Sea temperature is perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's clifftop or beachside bar. Enjoy a premium dinner at the resort's signature restaurant featuring locally sourced seafood and traditional Greek cuisine with a modern twist.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the resort's beachfront terrace – Greek yogurt with Cretan honey, fresh pastries, eggs Benedict, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and specialty Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch on the boat or at a seaside taverna near the resort – grilled octopus, tzatziki, saganaki, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Signature restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort – whole grilled sea bream with lemon and capers, slow-roasted lamb with herbs, and a curated selection from the Greek wine list

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Keep the pace relaxed. Ask the concierge to book upcoming experiences and restaurant reservations for the rest of the trip today.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour: Depart early with a private guide to explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets in Monastiraki. Taste cured meats, artisan cheeses, fresh olives, spices, and local street food. Engage with vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market tour, explore the Monastiraki and Plaka neighborhoods on foot. Visit curated boutique shops for premium Greek olive oils, wines, and artisan goods. Optional visit to the Acropolis Museum for cultural context, followed by a relaxed afternoon coffee at a rooftop café overlooking the Acropolis.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Athens' finest restaurants in the Kolonaki or Syntagma district. Return to the resort via private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Immersive tasting lunch during the food tour at Varvakios Agora – fresh seafood, grilled meats, traditional pies (spanakopita, tiropita), and local wine pairings
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hytra or Funky Gourmet (Michelin-starred) in Athens – contemporary Greek tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the Athens Central Market Food Tour with a premium private guide in advance. Private driver recommended for the full day. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Carry a small bag for market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or spa session at the Aegean Bliss Resort wellness center. Follow with a refreshing swim in the Aegean Sea from the private beach. The hot and sunny weather makes this a perfect beach morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class at a local culinary studio near the resort. Learn to prepare authentic Greek dishes such as moussaka, spanakopita, and loukoumades using fresh, locally sourced ingredients. This is an immersive premium food experience.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the meal you prepared during the cooking class in a private dining setting, paired with premium Greek wines selected by the instructor. Return to resort for a relaxing evening.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – fresh fruit platter, Greek yogurt parfait, warm croissants, and Greek mountain tea
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort – grilled halloumi salad, hummus with pita, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Private dining experience featuring the dishes prepared during the afternoon cooking class, paired with Assyrtiko white wine from Santorini and Agiorgitiko red from Nemea

day_by_day.notes: Book the private cooking class through the resort concierge. Classes are typically 3–4 hours and include a market visit to source ingredients. Dietary preferences should be communicated in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit: Take a premium private boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. Depart early to arrive before the crowds. Swim in the turquoise waters surrounded by dramatic white limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the private boat tour around Zakynthos, exploring the Blue Caves and other hidden sea caves along the northern coastline. Snorkeling in secluded bays with crystal-clear visibility. Onboard lunch served on the private yacht.
day_by_day.evening: Return from Zakynthos and enjoy a sunset dinner at a premium waterfront restaurant. Alternatively, dine at the resort with a specially arranged private beach dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure – energy-rich options including eggs, smoked salmon, avocado toast, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Gourmet onboard lunch on the private yacht – freshly prepared Greek salad, grilled shrimp skewers, stuffed vine leaves, local cheeses, and chilled Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort – candlelit table on the sand, grilled lobster, saffron risotto with seafood, and a premium Santorini wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach is only accessible by boat. Book a private luxury yacht charter for the most exclusive experience. Depart by 08:00 to beat crowds. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light cover-up. Check weather conditions the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and relaxation morning at the resort. Indulge in a premium spa treatment – choose from a traditional Greek olive oil massage, a thalassotherapy session, or a couple's spa ritual. Afterward, lounge by the infinity pool overlooking the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local winery or olive grove for a private guided tour and tasting. Learn about traditional Greek wine production and the importance of olive oil in Greek cuisine. Sample premium estate wines and extra-virgin olive oils with artisan bread and local accompaniments.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest village or town on foot. Browse local artisan shops, watch the sunset from a hilltop viewpoint, and enjoy a leisurely dinner at a highly regarded local taverna.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast – full spread including freshly baked bread, pastries, cold cuts, local honey, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Wine and olive oil tasting lunch at the estate – paired mezze including olives, aged cheeses, cured meats, and rustic bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at a renowned local taverna – slow-cooked lamb kleftiko, horiatiki salad with barrel-aged feta, and fresh baklava for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Ask the concierge to arrange a private winery or olive estate tour with transportation. Many estates require advance booking, especially for private tastings. Bring a small cooler bag if purchasing wine or olive oil to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip: Depart early by private vehicle to Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete (if accessible from your base), famous for its breathtaking pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise lagoon. Arrive early to enjoy the beach at its most serene before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon wading through the shallow lagoon, swimming in the warm Aegean waters, and exploring the small island connected by a shallow sandbar. Set up a premium beach setup with a private parasol, loungers, and a chilled drinks cooler arranged through your concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Return from Elafonissi and enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort or a nearby waterfront restaurant. Celebrate the midpoint of the trip with a bottle of premium Greek sparkling wine.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast – grab-and-go option with fresh pastries, fruit, and coffee in a premium packed breakfast if departing very early
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the beach at Elafonissi – premium hamper prepared by the resort including cold mezze, artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top-rated seafood restaurant near the resort – fresh catch of the day, grilled calamari, and a dessert of loukoumades with honey and cinnamon

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is best visited on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds. The pink sand coloring is most visible in the morning light. Wear water shoes as the lagoon floor can be uneven. Apply high-SPF sunscreen as the beach offers minimal shade.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise paddle-boarding or kayaking session along the coastline, arranged through the resort's water sports center. The calm morning sea and warm temperatures make this an idyllic experience. Follow with a refreshing outdoor shower and beachside breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cultural afternoon: Visit a nearby archaeological site, Byzantine church, or local museum to deepen your understanding of Greek history and culture. Private guided tour recommended for an enriched experience.
day_by_day.evening: Premium sunset cruise on a private sailing yacht along the coast. Watch the sun dip below the horizon with champagne in hand. Return to resort for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Beachside breakfast at the resort – smoothie bowls, avocado toast, Greek yogurt with pomegranate, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local village restaurant near the archaeological site – traditional Greek lunch spread including stuffed peppers, gigantes beans, and fresh village bread
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the resort's fine dining restaurant – tasting menu featuring seasonal Greek ingredients, paired with a curated 5-course wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Book the private sunset sailing cruise at least 2 days in advance through the resort concierge. Bring a light layer for the boat as the evening sea breeze can be cool after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the beach. Try snorkeling in the clear Aegean waters directly from the resort's private beach. The warm sea temperature (around 24–25°C) is ideal. Relax on a premium sun lounger with a good book and a fresh juice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private food and wine pairing masterclass at the resort or a nearby culinary venue. A sommelier and chef guide you through the art of pairing Greek wines (Assyrtiko, Xinomavro, Moschofilero) with traditional Greek dishes. An intimate and educational premium experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at an exclusive hilltop restaurant with panoramic sea views. Reserve a private table on the terrace for the most romantic and scenic setting.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – eggs your way, smoked salmon platter, fresh pastries, and a mimosa to start the day
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch – grilled vegetable antipasto, fresh hummus, and a chilled glass of Santorini Assyrtiko
meals.dinner: Hilltop restaurant dinner – slow-roasted suckling pig, wild greens with lemon dressing, and a rich Greek honey cake (melopita) for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The food and wine pairing masterclass should be booked through the resort. Groups are typically limited to 6–8 guests for an intimate experience. This is a highlight experience for food lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Morning hike or nature walk along a scenic coastal trail near the resort. A local guide can lead you through fragrant wild herbs, olive groves, and dramatic clifftop viewpoints. End the walk at a secluded cove for a private swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a luxurious afternoon at the spa. Indulge in a full body scrub using local sea salt and olive oil, followed by a relaxing hydrotherapy session. Spend the remaining afternoon by the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-villa or in-suite dinner experience. The resort chef prepares a bespoke multi-course Greek menu exclusively for you, served on your private terrace or balcony overlooking the sea.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the hike – hearty options including granola, boiled eggs, cheese, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at the secluded cove – artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, olives, and chilled water prepared by the resort
meals.dinner: Private in-suite dining experience – chef's bespoke 6-course tasting menu featuring the best of Greek seasonal produce, paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy walking shoes and a hat for the morning hike. Carry plenty of water as temperatures reach 29°C. The private in-suite dining experience is a must-book highlight – arrange with the resort at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby island or coastal town by private speedboat. Explore charming whitewashed streets, visit a local market, and browse artisan shops. Pick up premium local products such as saffron, thyme honey, and hand-painted ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lunch at the island's or town's best waterfront restaurant. Spend the afternoon exploring at a leisurely pace, swimming off a local beach, or simply sitting at a café and people-watching. Return to resort by private boat in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Enjoy pre-dinner drinks at the bar with live acoustic Greek music (if available), followed by dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – full buffet spread with a wide selection of Greek and international options
meals.lunch: Waterfront lunch at the island or coastal town – freshly caught grilled fish, Greek salad, and a carafe of local white wine
meals.dinner: Beachfront dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort – grilled king prawns with garlic and herbs, lamb chops with rosemary, and a classic Greek dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Ask the concierge to arrange a private speedboat for the day trip. Bring cash for local market purchases as some vendors may not accept cards. Light layers recommended for the boat ride.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning at the resort. Swim, snorkel, and soak in the last hours of warm Aegean sun. Treat yourself to a final spa treatment – perhaps a relaxing facial or foot massage to prepare for the journey home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping and exploration of the local area. Visit a high-end boutique for premium Greek jewelry, leather goods, or designer resort wear. Stop at a local deli to pick up vacuum-packed Greek specialties to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the finest restaurant available – either at the resort or a nearby acclaimed establishment. Celebrate the end of an extraordinary trip with a premium tasting menu and the best wines Greece has to offer.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the resort terrace – smoked salmon, fresh oysters, pastries, and a glass of sparkling wine to mark the final morning
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café or resort pool bar – mezze sharing platter and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner – premium tasting menu with dishes such as saffron-infused seafood risotto, Wagyu-style Greek beef, truffle-laced pasta, and a decadent chocolate and Greek honey dessert, paired with a full wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Pack non-essentials tonight to make the morning departure smoother. Confirm checkout time and airport transfer with the resort. Keep one outfit and essentials accessible for the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a last leisurely breakfast on the terrace with views of the Aegean Sea. Check out of the resort and transfer to the airport via private luxury vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, enjoy the airport's premium lounge facilities. Reflect on 13 unforgettable days in Greece.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Greece. Carry home memories of stunning beaches, extraordinary food, and the warm hospitality of the Greek islands.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – a full and indulgent spread to close the trip in style, including fresh pastries, Greek yogurt, seasonal fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Premium airport lounge dining or a light meal at an airport restaurant
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or upon arrival at home destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer the night before. Allow extra time at the airport for any last-minute duty-free shopping – Greece has excellent selections of olive oil, wines, and spirits to bring home. Confirm all luggage weight limits if purchasing bottles.
